comparator.name: Global Arts, Culture and Politics (BA Cultural Studies)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official current study-programme page publishes a complete 180-ECTS structure: a 60-ECTS common first year, a 60-ECTS second year consisting of a 48-ECTS major plus two six-ECTS common courses, and a 60-ECTS third year with research lab, elective/minor space and final project. The normalized Cultural Studies target does not privilege one of four majors, so Curating the Past is selected as the first option listed in the curriculum table; its internal courses are not invented because the page publishes only the 48-ECTS aggregate.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the broad accredited Cultural Studies degree and does not privilege one of the four majors. Curating the Past is the first option listed in the official second-year curriculum table and is therefore selected before comparison with UCR.

core: Global arts, culture, media and representation as ways of understanding political life
Global political power, social inequality, justice and cultural change
Cultural and humanities research through visual, archival, digital, rhetorical and interview methods
adjacent: Art, media, curating, heritage and global cultural histories
Sustainability, climate, ecology and environmental humanities
Artificial intelligence, platforms, media and algorithmic culture
questions: How do art, media and cultural representation shape political debate and social inequality?
How can culture and the arts respond to climate change, sustainability and social problems?
How do artificial intelligence and platforms transform everyday culture, ethics and politics?

alternatives.label: Global Arts, Culture & Politics
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly combines global culture, arts and media with politics, sociology and research methods; it does not imply UvA’s dedicated 48-ECTS major structure.
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible cultural-studies pathway combining media, rhetoric, sociology, politics, cultural representation, visual analysis, research methods and public-facing creative work.
progression: Communication, media, sociology, politics, psychology and qualitative and quantitative foundations precede advanced persuasion, organisational culture, media analysis, political study and creative production. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with nine 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Culture, Sustainability & Environmental Politics
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines climate, environmental governance and sustainability research with politics, law, economics and public communication.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced Reimagining Sustainability direction around climate, environmental systems, cultural and political change, law, economics, communication and applied sustainability research.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes sustainability, climate and environmental politics the central cultural challenge; it differs from both other programmes by well over four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Sustainability, politics, economics, sociology and data foundations precede environmental law, climate governance, advanced sustainability and applied environmental research. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: AI, Media & Algorithmic Culture
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly combines computing and data methods with media, communication, sociology and critical AI analysis.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced Human and Artificial Intelligence direction around programming, data science, AI ethics, media, platforms, communication, sociology and critical analysis of algorithmic culture.
alternatives.distinctness: This route centres AI, platforms, media and algorithmic culture; it differs from both the broad closest match and the sustainability route by well over four courses and 30 EC.
progression: Programming, mathematics, AI ethics, data and communication foundations precede machine learning, deep learning, optimisation, platform analysis and advanced media work. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.

blocks: Both introduce rhetorical analysis and purposive communication.
Both establish visual and media literacy for cultural analysis.
Both develop advanced persuasive communication and writing for audiences.
Both support advanced cultural and media production within a coherent thematic pathway.
Both introduce sociological approaches to culture, society and inequality.
Both introduce global political structures, power and conflict.
Both develop qualitative interviewing, observation and on-site research methods.
Both examine philosophical foundations of humanistic and social inquiry.
Both address ethical and societal consequences of artificial intelligence.

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme-defining global arts, culture, politics, media and representation interests. Sustainability/environmental politics and AI/algorithmic culture are the two strongest coherent remaining directions and yield feasible, substantively distinct programmes. Culture and social justice is already substantially covered by the closest match. Production stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

notes.text: The selected Curating the Past major is published as a single 48-ECTS aggregate. Its internal courses and credit distribution are not invented.

UvA integrates arts, cultural politics, practical skills and one 48-ECTS major in a dedicated Cultural Studies degree. UCR distributes related study across a student-designed 24-course Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum.
